note_add: Reservation fee: recreation.gov's site-wide policy says a reservation fee 'may be charged' ($8 online, $9 call centre, $3 in person), and whether it is depends on the agency: the Forest Service, BLM and others pass it on, while the Corps (by policy) and the Park Service (park by park) fold the cost into the nightly fee and charge none. So it is set on the agency rows, not here. Changing an individual-campsite reservation to dates entirely outside the original costs $10; extending or shortening it is free. A cancellation keeps back a $10 service fee. Cancelling the day before or the day of arrival costs $10 plus the first night (all of it for a one-night stay). The reservation fee itself is never refunded. Tax: not settled for federal campgrounds as a whole. Federally run fee campgrounds post untaxed FLREA fees, but concessionaire-run ones add state and local tax: the Forest Service's Pines Campground (Stanislaus) posts '$33.00 per night (+fees and taxes)', and Yellowstone's concession campgrounds post '+ taxes'. Non-resident: since 2026-01-01 eleven national parks charge non-US residents a $100 entrance surcharge. That is an entrance charge, not a camping rate, and it doesn't touch any US state's residents.

unsettled.reservation_fee: No single figure covers every federal entry. recreation.gov's policy says a fee 'may be charged' ($8/$9/$3), and in practice it depends on the agency: USFS charges $8 (federal:usfs), USACE charges none by policy (federal:usace), and NPS parks fold the cost into the nightly rate. Observed in recreation.gov's campground API: fee_model 1 on all 84 FS, 14 BLM, 1 BOR and 1 FWS facilities sampled, and fee_model 0 on all 54 USACE and 21 NPS facilities.
unsettled.tax: Federally run FLREA fees appear untaxed, but no primary source says so in as many words, and concessionaire-run USFS and NPS campgrounds add tax ('+fees and taxes', '+ taxes'). So {percent: 0} would be wrong for a large share of the federal rows. NOTE: the schema comment and docs/campground-schema.md §4.2 say 'federal fees are untaxed' as a flat fact, and these sources don't support that for concession campgrounds.
unsettled.nonresident: No federal camping rate depends on state residency (this row's existing note says so), but I found no explicit primary statement, so I wrote no zero. The 2026 NPS non-US-resident $100 surcharge is an entrance charge at 11 parks.
unsettled.entrance: Differs by agency: barred by statute on USFS/BLM/BOR land (set on those rows), per park for NPS, per refuge for FWS.
unsettled.extra_vehicle: Differs by agency and facility (USACE settled on its row).

note_add: Reservation fee: $8.00 per reservation, charged by recreation.gov (the Forest Service's fee-site notices say it 'is not a Forest Service recreation fee'). recreation.gov lists $9 by call centre and $3 in person. A first-come site paid on arrival has no reservation fee. Entrance: the law bars an entrance fee on Forest Service land. A standard amenity (day-use) fee can still apply on top of camping at a National Volcanic Monument, a National Conservation Area or a High Impact Recreation Area, set site by site; an entry inside one must carry it itself. Extra vehicles and people per site: set per campground (often an extra-vehicle fee and a 6- or 8-person cap). Tax: concessionaire-run campgrounds (most developed USFS campgrounds) usually add state and local tax ('+fees and taxes' at Pines, Stanislaus); Forest Service-run ones post untaxed fees, so tax is left unset.

note_add: Corps camping fees are per site and include the site's amenities, utilities and the cost of recreation.gov, so there is no reservation fee (recreation.gov's $10 change/cancellation service fees still apply). The camping permit covers the project's Corps-run day-use areas (boat ramps, beaches) on the days it is valid. Vehicles parked on the site within its posted carrying capacity (people, vehicles and camping units, set per site by the project, often 2 vehicles and 8 people) cost nothing extra. A vehicle in separate improved parking may be charged a parking fee, and a registered camper's day visitors may be charged up to 50% of the site fee. The site may not exceed its posted capacity, so there is no national max. Policy source: the USACE guide implementing EC 1130-2-550 Chapter 9 (2015; the fee structure took effect 2016-01-01). Its parking, day-use and per-site rules repeat ER 1130-2-550 ch. 9.

It shall also entitle the holder to use any or all Corps- operated day use facilities without paying additional use fees at the same project, on any day for which the permit is valid.

summary: Settled from the Corps' own fee guidance: no reservation fee (cost built into the per-site fee), no entrance or day-use fee for campers at the same project, no charge for people or for vehicles on the site within its posted capacity (overflow parking and day visitors may be charged; in the note). Senior/Access Pass gives a flat 50% at Corps-operated campgrounds, 'shall entitle', not at leaseholder or concessionaire parks. Tax is unsettled.

note_add: Entrance: the law bars an entrance fee on BLM land. Reservation fee: most reservable BLM campgrounds add recreation.gov's $8 ($9 by phone; e.g. Ken's Lake: '$20 per site per night plus reservation fee'). Some fold it into the nightly fee (Datil Well, NM, 2025 plan), so it is left per campground. Extra vehicles and people: per campground (Log Gulch, ID: each RV/trailer/tent $25, two per site).

note_add: Entrance: per park and paid on top of camping ('Camping fees are in addition to the standard Park Entrance Fee', Sleeping Bear Dunes). Most NPS sites charge none; where charged it runs up to $35 per private vehicle for 7 days. Since 2026-01-01, 11 parks add $100 for each non-US resident 16 and over (Acadia, Bryce Canyon, Everglades, Glacier, Grand Canyon, Grand Teton, Rocky Mountain, Sequoia & Kings Canyon, Yellowstone, Yosemite, Zion). Reservation fee: NPS campgrounds generally fold recreation.gov's $6-8 per-reservation cost into the nightly fee rather than charging it separately (Congaree: 'the park assumes these costs'; Gulf Islands: 'camping fees are used to cover this expense'). No agency-wide statement was found, so it is left unset. Tax: NPS-run campgrounds post untaxed fees, while concessioner-run ones add tax (Yellowstone: '$38 + taxes').

note_add: Reservation fee: C$11.50 online, C$13.50 by phone, per campsite per stay (a stay is consecutive nights at one park). Each change or cancellation is another C$11.50 online or C$13.50 by phone, plus other fees close to arrival. Fees include all applicable taxes. Entry: camping fees do not include park entry, and you need a valid entry pass for every day of the visit, whether or not you go in and out that day. It is charged at most places and varies by park: C$7.25-12.25 per adult or C$15.00-24.50 per family/group (up to seven people in one vehicle) a day in 2026, Kejimkujik and Pukaskwa lowest, Banff, Jasper, Pacific Rim and Gros Morne highest. Youth 17 and under are free, and a Discovery Pass (C$167.50 family/group) covers a year. Extra vehicles: set per campground (Bruce Peninsula, Cyprus Lake: C$14.75 a night). Fire permits are extra where sold (Banff C$12-17 a day). 2026 promotion: free admission and 25% off camping from June 19 to September 7, 2026. It is over, and regular fees apply from September 8, 2026.
